A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDGD method and VaLLu study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LVLM evaluations, hallucination analyses, component ablations, and VaLLu results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds caption-source, human-evaluation, computational-efficiency, and beam-search results.

M1.justification: Appendices C and N introduce optional variants using GPT-4 or SmallCap captions and applying VDGD reweighting before beam selection. These extend caption generation and decoding procedures while retaining the description prefix, plausibility constraint, and KL objective in Section 5.1.

E1.justification: The benchmark coverage, VaLLu composition, and evaluated task domains are retained. The added studies use existing coverage; changing caption generators or decoding settings does not introduce a new task or dataset.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator membership in the main and corresponding appendix comparisons is unchanged. Most instances of VDD are corrected to VCD, identifying the same baseline. CCoT, Visual Table, and Visual Evidence Prompting are newly discussed but not experimentally compared; external captioners appear as VDGD component variants.

E3.justification: Added experiments vary caption providers, test beam search on MMMU with LLaVA-v1 and LLaVA-1.5, and measure latency and FLOPs on LLaVA-1.5 using a 48GB GPU. Existing benchmark splits, default sampling settings, and human-evaluation sample limits are retained. Beam width and timing workload details are not supplied.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supporting validation through caption-source ablations, beam-search testing, and measured computational-cost analysis. It also supplies numerical evidence for the previously described no-image ablation and human/metric correlation analysis. Existing failure cases, hallucination analyses, and retrieval-k sensitivity tests remain.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly specifies that human scores are averaged over the five evaluators, and Table 4 details the original-metric/GPT/human correlation reporting. Both versions retain three-run averaging and the existing ablation uncertainty notation; additional runs or a new uncertainty-estimation practice are not established.

E6.justification: Main Table 2 and the matched appendix benchmark scores are unchanged, but substantial supporting results are added. Table 3 adds GPT-caption, SmallCap-caption, and no-image scores; for LLaVA-1.5 these are 2.91, 2.38, and 1.95 against the retained VDGD score of 2.64. Tables 4, 14, and 15 add human/metric comparisons, correlations, computational measurements, and beam-search scores. Table 15's LLaVA-v1 VDGD reference score of 1.42 conflicts with Table 2's retained 1.49.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(3), Algorithm 1, and Appendix E's complexity derivation remain unchanged. Section 3.3 shifts rank thresholds from one-based to zero-based indexing, consistent with the existing BR > 0 classifier; this is an indexing correction rather than a new mathematical classification or derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about the visual perception gap, training-free VDGD, 2%-33% improvements, and the VaLLu contribution remain. The contribution list is shortened, and the placeholder X benchmarks becomes 8, specifying the already reported evaluation rather than expanding its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets improved GPT-generated captions as implicit knowledge transfer and presents smaller captioners as an efficiency alternative. Appendix M adds an argument for practical computational costs. Section 6 removes the alignment/RAG future-work item while retaining the inaccurate-description and double-prompting limitations.

D1.justification: v3 documents external caption-provider identities and hardware for the new timing comparison. Access instructions change to a project page, and the promised post-acceptance code/checkpoint release statement is removed; actual online availability cannot be established from the PDFs. The main-text VCD caption-generation disclosure disappears, although Appendix C retains the corresponding minus-VCD ablation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against CCoT, Visual Table, and Visual Evidence Prompting, emphasizing representations, training requirements, and abstract-image applicability. References additionally introduce the Bai et al. survey and Ramos et al.'s SmallCap, while new Appendix O extends the hallucination-related discussion. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: Changes include a compressed contribution list, expanded related-work and ablation explanations, new Appendices M-O, author/contact edits, and corrected cross-references. Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. A new editorial error replaces the Style Hallucinations label with 1.3 Hallucinations.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains three rows, and Tables 4, 14, and 15 are added. Subsequent tables are renumbered, several captions are corrected, and appendix material reflows. Figures 1-41 and the overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously asserted validation more inspectable through the missing no-image ablation scores and detailed human/metric comparison, while adding useful caption-source and efficiency checks. These benefits are limited by incomplete new protocol details and reporting inconsistencies: Appendix M gives VDGD latency as 2.5 seconds versus Table 14's 2.4, and Table 15's LLaVA-v1 reference score differs from Table 2. The additions provide a limited net improvement in evidential transparency.
